name: Halo Ube-Coconut Meltaways
description: Pastel-violet discs that dissolve slowly on the tongue, releasing layered ube and toasted coconut notes. Halcyon markets these as 'a moment of stillness' — they contain trace ashwagandha and L-theanine for a mild calm effect.
flavor_profile: Creamy ube earthiness, sweet coconut milk finish, faint vanilla undertone; smooth, non-gritty dissolution
cultural_context: Halo Meltaways occupy a cultural middle ground between candy and mood supplement. Workers on long shifts pop them openly. Tier 3 professionals keep a tin on their desk as a stress signal — if the tin is out, you're having a day.
story_hooks: The 'trace calm compounds' in a factory batch have been quietly doubled by a disgruntled line chemist — the candy is now producing noticeable sedation, and Halcyon's risk team needs to quietly recall it without triggering a regulatory audit.
A BCI-integrated user reports that Halo Meltaways produce a synesthetic color bloom when consumed while in deep interface — Halcyon has no idea why and wants the data suppressed.
A Tier 3 therapist prescribes Halo Meltaways to a patient instead of a licensed mood regulator to avoid putting it in their corporate health file.
